T1.structure: Responsive six-slot single-selection grid, long details and global safety disclosure; genuine two-column/one-column distinction.
T1.businessAndRoutes: P1/P2/H1 selected summaries, a selected state, enablement, disclosure labels and five stimulus-bound callback expectations agree with the public behavior. 7 selected states and 9 actions per case.
T1.hiddenFairness: Same rule identities and methods; changed labels and dark/RTL/intermediate-width/font combination stay inside publicly allowed data/environment rules.

T2.structure: Eager chronological one-column timeline with selected inline dossier and external global disclosure. The structure differs materially from the grid, subject to resolving B2.
T2.businessAndRoutes: P1/P2/H1 selected business values and successful callback action indices agree. 7 states and 9 actions per case. The route does not certify dossier migration while remaining open; that remains a full-brief obligation.
T2.hiddenFairness: Heldout labels/environment change without adding a new rule, callback meaning or method.

T3.structure: Grouped six-service multi-selection checklist with ordered-label/minute sum, caller reset to a subset and global handover disclosure. It introduces substantive set/aggregate behavior beyond the other two tasks.
T3.businessAndRoutes: P1/P2/H1 aggregate summaries and sums, a selected state, enablement, labels and callback indices agree. 7 states and 10 actions per case. Deselection is expressly outside the selected ledger.
T3.hiddenFairness: Changed labels/minutes and permitted dark/RTL/font/width combination remain within public sum, ordering, selection and environment rules.

blockers.title: Unavailable reason has no supplied data or fixed meaning

locations.pointer: line 10: Unavailable entries remain visible with a reason; model can disable any entry at replacement
line 10: Unavailable entries remain visible with a reason; model can disable any entry at replacement
line 10: Unavailable entries remain visible with a reason; model can disable any entry at replacement

blockers.reason: The brief requires a reason, but item models carry only available, label and ordinary detail (plus severity/minutes where applicable). Neither the disabled station/service detail nor the newly disabled a supplies an unavailability reason. The drawings append Unavailable, which is a status rather than a reason. A builder must invent product information or silently weaken the brief. River severity/incident condition is also not a defined availability-reason mapping, especially when a watch incident is disabled by replacement. This is a full-brief implementability issue even though it is outside the selected disabled-enabled atom.
blockers.minimalRevision: In a new sealed revision, either explicitly require only the fixed Unavailable status label, matching the present API/reference, or add a typed reason field and independently supplied values/display rules to the public API, cases, bridges and references. Do not let implementations invent reasons.

blockers.title: Timeline marker placement conflicts with the structural reference

locations.pointer: line 8: leading rail and time/severity marker sit outside each select button
line 1: first card rect x=28 y=282.2 width=314 height=86.8; time label x=48 y=314.2; WATCH x=48 y=341; rail path x=21

blockers.reason: The reference puts both the time-bearing label and severity inside the colored selectable card; only the rail is outside. There is no distinct external time/severity marker in the SVG or PNG. As API.md binds choice IDs to actual selection buttons, the brief and visual hierarchy leave two competing structures for the implementer/reviewer. An unlabelled assumption about an invisible inner activation boundary would not resolve that independently.
blockers.minimalRevision: Choose the intended hierarchy before implementation. The smallest consistent wording is to keep only the non-interactive rail outside and explicitly put the time-bearing label and severity inside the single selection button, as drawn. If external markers are intended, revise the drawings and specify their data/activation boundary instead.

blockers.title: Wrapping proposition does not distinguish intentional hidden text from unreadable text

locations.pointer: lines 8 and 12: details only in expanded selected dossier

blockers.reason: The Boolean asks whether all choice labels/details and disclosure-content words are readable. It is selected true at closed baseline/submitted states, and T2 deliberately hides all unselected incident details even when expanded. One literal reading fails correct intentional disclosure hiding; another reading silently restricts the question to the currently required visible content. The exact-state phrase does not define that quantifier. It can also make missing disclosure content indistinguishable from a wrapping pass.
blockers.minimalRevision: State explicitly that the wrapping atom evaluates only text required to be visible under the current selection/disclosure rules; intentional hidden content is excluded. Specify how missing required text is treated, without allowing it to count as correct wrapping. Keep wrapping and overlap separate, and preserve U for incomplete coverage. Re-source the public/private propositions and locks in a new sealed revision.

nonblocking.title: Make the outside-ledger disclosure task-specific
nonblocking.reason: The generic limits list is useful but does not expressly name the core structural properties that these 14 rules do not certify: T1 column switch/reading hierarchy, T2 rail/dossier location and dossier migration, T3 group membership/full-width estimate structure. Wrapping and overlap do not certify those properties.
nonblocking.suggestion: Add an explicit task-specific list of those unselected obligations. This does not require expanding the selected score or simplifying the UI.

nonblocking.title: Remove unused event expectations from non-stimulus states
nonblocking.reason: These unused typed values contain future submission events despite the contract marking the corresponding successful-activation cells N/A. They do not affect the generated assertions, but are misleading reference data.
nonblocking.suggestion: Remove or explicitly label unused values in a new revision; keep the current correct N/A and successful-stimulus gate.

nonblocking.reason: The station/service briefs retain incident/dossier/T2 language, and the multi-select API retains a nullable-selection sentence although it uses a non-null list. Exact signatures and fixtures are consistent, so these are editorial issues.
nonblocking.suggestion: Use task-local terms and list-selection wording; define what normal/enlarged text means if broader full-brief combinations are later assessed.

processDeviation.explanation: During gate-integrity checking, the first loop traversed the entire candidate-v8 member file list, which also contains non-allowlisted entries. Their raw bytes went only to SHA256; no such file was decoded or printed, and no contents informed the findings. Stored per-file results were narrowed to candidate-v8/. This is disclosed rather than asserting perfect read-scope compliance. No assignment, other review, old task or defect text was inspected.
